title: Gate driver PCB layout
purpose: Convert a gate-driver schematic into placement, stack-up, routing and isolation constraints with low-inductance gate loops and intact isolation barriers.
applicable_conditions: Isolated SiC gate drivers on multilayer PCBs
Drivers on the power board or on plug-in driver boards
not_applicable: Numeric creepage/clearance values (taken from the governing standard)
principles: Power commutation loop has priority over the gate loop
Gate and Kelvin source as adjacent-layer pours with Kelvin shielding
Decoupling capacitors inside the gate loop
Driver adjacent to its switch; connectors dominate inductance
No copper crossing isolation barriers on any layer
Differential pairs and short single-ended segments with filters at receivers
procedure: Assign nets to spacing classes and create class-pair clearance rules
Place power stage and HF capacitors, then drivers at their switches
Place bias supplies inside islands with CM choke order
Add V_GS probe point at device side of R_G
Run DRC and inspect every copper layer
component_considerations: Connector inductance for plug-in drivers; MMCX for V_GS
Bias transformer/module pin spacing for creepage
verification_methods: Netlist check that Kelvin and power source nets are distinct
Extract driver-to-device distance and decoupling loop
known_limitations: TI layout observations are visual only
Manufacturer guidance not quantified by AIPE parasitic extraction
